_about: Major copper mine supply disruptions used for the event study on the Drivers tab (scripts/drivers_analysis.py). 'date' is the day the news reached the market (if it broke after the US session, the next day). 'share' is the mine's approximate share of world mine supply, %. Add a row to include a new event; the analysis reruns with the market data.

events.what: About 2,500 workers strike at the world's largest copper mine after contract talks fail; lasted 43-44 days.
Freeport declares force majeure on Grasberg concentrate shipments after a five-week Indonesian export ban.
More than 3,000 unionised workers walk off at Codelco's Chuquicamata; mine runs at about 50% for two weeks.
MMG announces it will halt Las Bambas from April 20 after community members occupy the mine.
MMG warns Las Bambas will halt production from February 1 as nationwide protests block supplies.
First Quantum halts production as a port blockade cuts power-plant supplies; on Nov 28 the Supreme Court rules the contract unconstitutional and the mine stays shut.
Union No. 1 (about 2,400 workers) strikes after pay talks fail; a deal ends it within days.
Ivanhoe announces underground mining at Kakula is suspended after seismic activity; 2025 guidance later withdrawn.
A tunnel collapse at Codelco's El Teniente on the evening of July 31 kills six workers and halts mining. Copper had crashed the day before on US tariff news.
About 800,000 tonnes of wet material floods the Grasberg Block Cave; operations suspended.
Freeport declares force majeure and says Grasberg won't be back to full output until 2027 (same disruption as Sep 8; windows overlap).
Union No. 2 strikes; Capstone runs the mine at up to 30% of normal output until early February.
Two unions (709 workers) at Antofagasta's Centinela go on strike after failed talks.
Codelco shuts the Andina concentrator after a tailings spill reaches the Blanco River.
